sections.label: MOH public health measures powers
sections.summary: It empowers MOH to undertake public health measures to prevent importation and spread of infectious diseases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It empowers the Ministry of Health (MOH) to undertake a range of public health measures to prevent the importation and spread of infectious diseases.

sections.label: Part 7 enacted in 2020
sections.summary: Part 7 of the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act was enacted in 2020 to complement the IDA and give MOH additional powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Part 7 of the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act – in short, I will refer to it as Part 7 – was, therefore, enacted in this House in 2020 to complement the IDA and provided additional powers to MOH to combat the pandemic.

sections.label: Part 7 temporary and expiring
sections.summary: Part 7 was intended to be temporary and will expire next month, which is why this Bill is tabled today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: A key motivation behind the recommendation is that while Part 7 served us well for COVID-19, it was intended to be temporary and, in fact, it will expire next month which is why we have to table this Bill today after the Committee of Supply.

sections.label: Minister declares PHT or PHE
sections.summary: The IDA will enable the Minister for Health to declare a Public Health Threat or PHE depending on severity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The IDA will therefore enable the Minister for Health to declare either a Public Health Threat (PHT) or PHE, depending on the severity of the situation.

sections.label: Minister declares PHE conditions
sections.summary: The amended IDA lets the Minister declare a PHE if an infectious disease seriously threatens public health and meets stated risk conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The amended IDA will empower the Minister to declare a PHE if he or she is satisfied that the actual or likely incidence and transmission of an infectious disease in Singapore constitutes a serious threat to public health and he additionally finds that the disease poses a substantial risk of either: one, a significant number of fatalities or incidents of serious disability of persons in Singapore; or two, a severe shortage or impairment of healthcare services and supplies in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: First, based on the current PHE powers in the IDA, the Minister will be able to declare the whole of or any area in Singapore to be a restricted zone and impose curfew-like measures in those zones.

sections.label: Requisition of resources under RORA
sections.summary: The Minister for Health will be able to exercise powers under RORA to requisition resources to secure human life and health.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Second, the Minister for Health will be able to exercise relevant powers under the Requisition of Resources Act 1985 (RORA) for the requisition of necessary resources to secure the safety of human life and health.

sections.label: PHT and PHE declaration duration
sections.summary: PHT and PHE declarations can last up to 90 days and the duration is extendable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: PHT and PHE declarations can be in force for a duration of up to 90 days and the duration is extendable.

sections.label: Public Health Threat and Emergency tiers
sections.summary: The third tier, Public Health Threat, covers situations needing wider or longer measures, while the fourth, Public Health Emergency, allows stricter measures like curfews or requisition of resources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Third tier is "Public Health Threat", which I have described to be for situations that may require more widespread or prolonged measures, up to and including those that were imposed during the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Fourth, "Public Health Emergency", being the most dire of public health crises where even stricter measures, such as curfews or requisition of resources, may be implemented.

sections.label: Deletion of contact tracing data
sections.summary: As of 1 February 2024, COVID-19 personal contact tracing data from TraceTogether and SafeEntry has been deleted, except TraceTogether data for a May 2020 murder case retained indefinitely by Police, and Part 11 will be repealed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As of 1 February 2024, all COVID-19 related personal contact tracing data derived from TraceTogether and SafeEntry has been deleted; with the exception of TraceTogether data pertaining to a murder case in May 2020, which will be retained by the Police indefinitely.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: With the deactivation of TraceTogether and SafeEntry, and the deletion of personal contact tracing data, Part 11 is no longer required and we will therefore repeal it.

sections.label: Minister may direct contact tracing
sections.summary: The Minister may direct all persons or any class of persons in charge of premises, such as shopping mall owners, to implement contact tracing or surveillance measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: One, the Minister may direct all persons or any class of persons in charge of premises, such as the owners of shopping malls, to implement contact tracing or surveillance measures.

sections.label: Higher penalty for repeat offenders
sections.summary: A higher maximum penalty can be provided for repeat offenders who do not comply with PHT or PHE regulations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Three, a higher maximum penalty can be provided for repeat offenders who do not comply with PHT or PHE regulations.

sections.label: Statutory appeals temporarily suspended
sections.summary: To focus resources on the pandemic response, statutory appeals to the Minister will be temporarily suspended during a PHT and PHE.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Four, to focus our resources on the pandemic response, statutory appeals to the Minister will be temporarily suspended during a PHT and PHE.

sections.label: Expanding pool of Health Officers
sections.summary: Clause 4 expands the pool of people who can be appointed as Health Officers to implement and enforce the IDA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill thus expands the pool of people who can be appointed as Health Officers to implement and enforce the IDA.

sections.label: Minister specifying travel health requirements
sections.summary: Clause 27 empowers the Minister to specify pre-departure or onboard health requirements for persons travelling to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As circumstances may differ in future outbreaks, clause 27 of the Bill introduces new provisions to empower the Minister to specify pre-departure or onboard health requirements which persons travelling to Singapore are required to comply with.

sections.label: Land travellers and pre-departure examinations
sections.summary: Clause 28 expands section 31 to include land travellers, and clause 32 removes the PHE prerequisite for pre-departure medical examinations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To guard against new diseases and to capture all possible modalities of travel into Singapore, clause 28 of the Bill will expand section 31 to include travellers entering Singapore by land.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Besides strengthening our levers to prevent the importation of diseases into Singapore, Singapore should also be responsible in preventing the exportation of diseases if we are experiencing an outbreak.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Therefore, clause 32 of the Bill removes the prerequisite under section 45B of the IDA for a PHE to be declared before the Minister can require persons to undergo medical examinations before leaving Singapore.

sections.label: Introducing at-risk individual concept
sections.summary: Clause 2 supplements three categories by introducing the concept of an at-risk individual.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 pandemic showed that there may be situations where we will need to take public health measures pre-emptively for persons who do not fall within any of these three categories, but are still at a higher risk of exposure to infection and onward transmission of the disease due to their unique circumstances and the nature of that particular disease.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Hence, clause 2 of the Bill supplements these three categories by introducing the concept of an "at-risk individual".

sections.label: Offence of risking household members
sections.summary: Clause 20 amends section 21A to make it an offence to deliberately or recklessly put another person in one's residence at risk of infection.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Additionally, there may also be cases where a person behaves irresponsibly inside their home to the detriment of other household members.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Hence, clause 20 of the Bill amends section 21A by additionally making it an offence to deliberately or recklessly put another person in one’s own place of residence at risk of infection by one’s own conduct.

sections.label: Public health assessment powers transfer
sections.summary: Powers under the IDA involving public health assessment will now reside with the Director-General of Health instead of the Minister for Health.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The powers under the IDA that involve public health assessment will now reside with the Director-General of Health instead of the Minister for Health.

sections.label: HIV disclosure exclusion amendment
sections.summary: The Bill excludes persons living with HIV from section 23(1) disclosure if they maintain an undetectable viral load, with conditions set out in subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The amendment Bill introduces a provision which excludes persons living with HIV from the disclosure requirement under section 23(1), if the person has maintained an undetectable viral load for a certain period of time preceding the sexual activity in question.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: A person is presumed to have done so if certain conditions are met.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: These conditions are that the person living with HIV adhere to treatment, have stable and consistent undetectable viral load test results from a licensed laboratory in Singapore, and have an undetectable viral load test result within a specified period prior to sexual activity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: More details will be set out in subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: This amendment aligns with medical advancements and our public health objective to curb transmission by shifting greater responsibility to individuals to get tested and treated for HIV in order to achieve and maintain a stable undetectable viral load.

sections.label: Other jurisdictions removed disclosure requirement
sections.summary: Sweden, Taiwan and the United States have removed the disclosure requirement for persons living with HIV who have no risk of transmitting HIV.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Other jurisdictions such as Sweden, Taiwan, United States have removed the disclosure requirement for persons living with HIV who have no risk of transmitting HIV.

sections.label: IDA amendments for future pandemics
sections.summary: The amendments enhance the IDA, port over COVID-19 Act Part 7 provisions, and align HIV disclosure requirements with scientific developments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We have sought to enhance the IDA to enable the swift prevention and control of infectious diseases, and the flexibility to calibrate our response according to the public health situation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We have ported over relevant provisions under the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act, Part 7, which served us well and updated the existing IDA provisions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The intent behind these amendments is to better equip MOH and Singapore to tackle future outbreaks and pandemics, safeguard the lives of our people and the functioning of our healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: I ask for the support of all Members for this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill will enhance the Government’s powers to deal with future pandemics, introduce more nuanced public health measures and align HIV disclosure requirements with scientific developments.

sections.label: Section 23 amendment and UN targets
sections.summary: The amendment recognises undetectable equals untransmittable, but a Member is concerned it does not go far enough towards UN AIDS 90-90-90 targets.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For too long, the law has lagged behind medical developments and the proposed amendment to section 23 will recognise the recognised principle "U equals U", or undetectable equals untransmittable.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, I am concerned that the proposed amendment to section 23 does not go far enough to assist in our journey towards the UN AIDS 90-90-90 targets for 90% of people living with HIV knowing their status, 90% of people living with HIV who know their status being on antiretroviral therapy and 90% of people living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy achieving viral suppression.

sections.label: Plan to repeal section 23
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Government plans to eventually do away with section 23, given expert consensus on criminal law's ineffectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In light of the consensus among public health experts on the ineffectiveness of criminal law in ending HIV, does the Government plan to eventually do away with section 23?

sections.label: Section 23(1) convictions 2015-2023
sections.summary: From 2015 to 2023, seven people were convicted under section 23(1); four had undetectable viral loads and all four had aggravating circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In relation to the queries on the prosecution, from 2015 to 2023, seven people were convicted under section 23(1) for failing to inform their sexual partners of the risk of getting HIV infection from them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Of the seven, four had undetectable viral loads at the time of their offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: All four convictions had aggravating circumstances, including simultaneous offences under the Misuse of Drugs Act; committing a second offence while under investigation for a first offence; one victim was a minor; and one deceived and exploited a victim by lying and posing as a police officer.

sections.label: HIV transmission risk criteria
sections.summary: Persons living with HIV meeting criteria, including an undetectable viral load test within nine months, would have effectively zero transmission risk, with criteria set out in subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Second, their most recent undetectable viral load test result should be nine months or less before the sexual activity in question.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Persons living with HIV who have met these criteria would have effectively zero risk of transmitting HIV to their sexual partner.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We will set out the criteria in subsidiary legislation, to allow for timely and responsive adjustments should the state of medical science change in the future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will allow Singapore to respond more nimbly to future infectious diseases threats, by providing the flexibility to calibrate our measures in accordance with the public health situation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The world remains vigilant against the next infectious disease threat; likewise, we must stand ready.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: I am confident that with these amendments, Singapore will be better equipped to tackle future outbreaks and pandemics and safeguard the health of our population.

sections.label: Four alert levels replace DORSCON
sections.summary: Four alert levels, Baseline, Outbreak, Threat and Emergency, will replace DORSCON for internal planning and external communications, as agreed through the Homefront Crisis Executive Group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: With this change, now that we have the new Act, we have four levels of alerts, which is: Baseline, Outbreak, Threat and Emergency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think it is more intuitive and clearer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, amongst the agencies, through our Homefront Crisis Executive Group (HCEG), we agreed that this new four tiers will replace DORSCON, both for internal planning as well as our external communications.

sections.label: Complaint evidence of undetectable viral load
sections.summary: When a complaint is made, the person investigated for the offence would have to produce the necessary evidence or show undetectable viral load.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: In relation to her point, actually how this works is that when a complaint is made, the person investigated for the offence would then have to produce the necessary evidence or show undetectable viral load (UVL) that they have had.

sections.label: Criminalisation of non-disclosure amendments
sections.summary: The amendments consider established scientific evidence that transmission risk with an undetectable viral load is effectively zero.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: On the second question on the criminalisation of non-disclosure, the amendments consider the established scientific evidence that transmission risk with an undetectable viral load is effectively zero.
